prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

WASHINGTON (CNN)  -- While nearly all maritime activity on the Potomac River will be halted on Inauguration Day, a handful of Mall-goers will sail from Virginia to Washington on water taxis. Some people will cross the Potomac River via water taxi on Inauguration Day. Working closely with the United States Coast Guard, the Potomac Riverboat Company, based in Alexandria, Virginia, plans to ferry up to 3,200 passengers from across the frigid Potomac on seven climate-controlled boats. The service is partially a response to the closure of all bridges from Virginia to D.C. on Inauguration Day, a measure that prompted an uproar among Virginia residents. According to maritime authorities in charge of the region, PRC is the only company being allowed to taxi across the river on the 20th. "Because the taxi service provided us with a security plan that we examined and deemed adequate to provide good security, I granted them a waiver to operate at an increased security level," National Capitol Region Port Captain Brian Kelley says. "The taxis are going to operate on a strict schedule and a strict route." The Coast Guard established a temporary security zone on waterways in the National Capitol Region, stepping up restrictions day-by-day leading up to 11 p.m. on January 19. At that point, all vessels must be docked and only boats with an approved sail plan will be allowed to operate. John Lake, a ship captain and the general manager of the company, said the sail plan he submitted was approved only a week ago and details nearly every move taxis will make. "All the departures are scheduled times. And those departures are supposed to leave on-time," Lake said. "We have to call in on each departure to the Coast Guard, let them know we're preparing to get under way, and get the permission, basically, to get under way." The boats depart the Alexandria Marina for the 40-minute trip beginning around 6 a.m. and must be docked on the southwest D.C. shore by 10 a.m. From there, it's a cold, mile-long walk to the Mall, so Lake has some advice for passengers. "Show up early to get through the security check and dress warm," he said. "It's going to be nice and toasty on the boat, but not so much outside." Return trips, tentatively scheduled for around 6 p.m., are not allowed to depart D.C. until after the inaugural parade events have concluded and President Obama is secured. In keeping with the Coast Guard's security measures, Lake says all passengers must arrive at least an hour early for a full screening. Passengers that want to stay in D.C. after the early evening departures will have to find other transport back across the Potomac. PRC Vice President Charlotte Hall says tickets went on sale Monday and the initial response from customers has been enthusiastic.

The Coast Guard has established a temporary security zone on waterways in the National Capitol Region, increasing restrictions day by day leading up to 11 p.m. on January 19. At that point, all vessels must be docked, and only boats with an approved sail plan will be permitted to operate.

John Lake, a ship captain and the company’s general manager, said the sail plan he submitted was approved only a week ago and details nearly every move the taxis will make.

“All the departures are scheduled times. And those departures are supposed to leave on time,” Lake said. “We have to call in on each departure to the Coast Guard, let them know we’re preparing to get under way, and get the permission, basically, to get under way.”

The boats will depart the Alexandria Marina for the 40-minute trip beginning around 6 a.m. and must be docked on the southwest Washington shore by 10 a.m. From there, passengers will face a cold, mile-long walk to the Mall, so Lake has some advice: “Show up early to get through the security check and dress warm,” he said. “It’s going to be nice and toasty on the boat, but not so much outside.”

Return trips, tentatively scheduled for around 6 p.m., will not be permitted to leave Washington until the inaugural parade events have concluded and President Obama has been secured. Passengers who wish to remain in Washington after the early-evening departures will have to find other transportation back across the Potomac.

The Potomac Riverboat Company, located in Alexandria, Virginia, is working in coordination with the U.S. Coast Guard to carry as many as 3,200 passengers across the cold Potomac River using seven heated boats. The service is being offered in part because every bridge from Virginia into Washington, D.C., will be closed that day, a decision that angered many Virginia residents.

Regional maritime officials say PRC is the only company that has been given permission to operate taxi service across the river on January 20.

The Coast Guard has created a temporary security area covering waterways in the National Capitol Region, with rules becoming tighter each day until 11 p.m. on January 19. After that time, every vessel must be tied up at a dock unless it has an authorized sail plan.

“All the departures are scheduled times. And those departures are supposed to leave on-time,” Lake said. “We have to call in on each departure to the Coast Guard, let them know we’re preparing to get under way, and get the permission, basically, to get under way.”

The boats will leave from the Alexandria Marina starting at about 6 a.m. for the 40-minute ride and must be docked along the southwest Washington shoreline by 10 a.m. Passengers will then face a chilly walk of about one mile to reach the Mall, prompting Lake to offer some practical guidance.

“Show up early to get through the security check and dress warm,” he said. “It’s going to be nice and toasty on the boat, but not so much outside.”

The return trips are expected to begin around 6 p.m., but boats may not leave Washington until the inaugural parade events are finished and President Obama has been secured.

Lake said that, in line with Coast Guard security rules, all passengers need to arrive at least one hour ahead of time for a complete screening. Anyone who chooses to remain in Washington after the early evening departures will need to arrange another way to get back across the Potomac.

**CNN —** Water taxis on the Potomac River will be allowed to carry passengers from Virginia into Washington, D.C., on President Obama’s Inauguration Day, despite tight security restrictions that will close much of the river to regular boat traffic, officials said.

The U.S. Coast Guard, which is enforcing a security zone around the nation’s capital for the January 20 ceremony, has approved limited ferry service for authorized water taxis operating between Virginia and the District. The decision gives some inauguration-goers another way to reach Washington as officials prepare for massive crowds and major road, bridge and transit restrictions.

Under the Coast Guard’s security plan, recreational vessels and most private boats will be barred from restricted areas of the Potomac near the inaugural events. But approved commercial operators will be permitted to run specific routes, subject to security screening and operational controls.

Officials said the water taxis must follow designated paths and schedules, and passengers may be subject to inspection before boarding. The vessels will be monitored as part of a broad security effort involving the Coast Guard, Secret Service, local police and other agencies.

Transportation officials have urged people attending the inauguration to use public transit, walk where possible and plan for long delays. Several bridges from Virginia into Washington are expected to have limited access, with many streets near the National Mall closed to traffic.

The allowance for water taxis could help ease pressure on crowded Metro stations and roadways, particularly for passengers coming from Alexandria and other Virginia waterfront areas.

Obama’s inauguration is expected to draw one of the largest crowds ever assembled in Washington, prompting an unprecedented transportation and security operation across the region.

**WASHINGTON —** With major Potomac River bridges closed for Inauguration Day security, a limited water taxi service is operating Monday to move ticketed passengers between Virginia and the District, under strict Coast Guard rules and enhanced screening procedures.

Company officials said the service is intended to provide a narrow transportation option for riders affected by bridge closures, not a general sightseeing route. Boats are operating on a reduced schedule and only between approved docks, with all trips subject to federal security restrictions on the river.

The U.S. Coast Guard has established security zones on the Potomac and Anacostia rivers for inauguration activities, limiting vessel movement near key government areas and bridge approaches. Commercial operators must follow assigned routes, maintain radio contact, and comply with law-enforcement instructions. Unauthorized vessels, anchoring, loitering, or deviation from approved paths are prohibited in restricted areas.

“This is a controlled operation from start to finish,” said a company operations official. “We are only running the trips that have been cleared, and passengers should expect airport-style patience — screening, lines and possible delays.”

Under the company’s procedures, passengers must have advance tickets and a valid government-issued photo ID. Bags are subject to inspection before boarding. Weapons, fireworks, drones, large coolers, alcohol, and oversized bags are not permitted. Officials said riders should arrive at least 45 minutes before departure to allow time for screening.

The limited schedule includes early inbound trips to Washington before the ceremony and afternoon outbound service after security restrictions begin easing. Company officials said boats will not wait for late passengers and may be delayed or canceled if ordered by the Coast Guard or other law-enforcement agencies.

A sample schedule provided by the operator listed morning departures from Virginia docks beginning around 6 a.m., with additional trips through midmorning. Return service was scheduled to begin in the afternoon and continue into the early evening, depending on river conditions and security clearance. Passengers were urged to check the company’s website or text alerts before traveling to the dock.

“We want people to understand that this is not normal commuter service,” said a company spokesperson. “Capacity is limited, the route is limited, and every trip depends on the security posture on the river.”

The company said passengers should dress for cold weather, as waiting areas may be outdoors, and should plan for additional walking once they arrive in the District because road closures and pedestrian checkpoints remain in place near the National Mall and downtown security perimeter.

Officials also warned that the water taxi will not provide access inside restricted zones unless passengers have proper inauguration credentials.

“If you do not have the right ticket or credential for the area you are trying to reach, the boat ride will not change that,” the spokesperson said. “People should map their route all the way from the dock to their final destination before they leave home.”

The Coast Guard said enforcement of the river security zones will continue throughout the inauguration period, with patrol boats positioned along the Potomac. Boaters who violate restrictions may be stopped, escorted out of the area, cited, or face further penalties.

Company officials said they expect heavy demand but cannot add trips unless federal authorities approve them.

“Our crews are ready, but the river is part of the security plan,” the operations official said. “Safety and compliance come first.”

The trip from Alexandria to Washington is expected to take roughly **45 minutes to an hour**, depending on river traffic, security checks and docking conditions. Riders are being advised to arrive early, carry identification and limit personal belongings to speed up screening.

The boats are expected to deliver passengers to a D.C. waterfront location within walking distance of the National Mall and inauguration events, though attendees should still plan for additional time to pass through pedestrian checkpoints and security perimeters once ashore.

Return service may be more complicated.

Due to federal security restrictions on the river and around D.C. after the ceremony, the Potomac Riverboat Company has warned that **return trips may be limited, delayed or unavailable at certain times**. Passengers may not be able to rely on an immediate boat ride back to Alexandria and should have a backup plan, such as Metro, rideshare service outside restricted zones or other regional transportation options.

Officials say the ferry option could help reduce pressure on roads and rail stations, but they caution that inauguration travel will still require patience and planning.

Attendees are encouraged to check the company’s latest schedule, ticket requirements and security guidance before traveling, as operations could change based on instructions from the U.S. Coast Guard, Secret Service or local authorities.

**Water Taxi Offers Virginia Residents an Alternative Route to Obama Inauguration**

As thousands of Virginians prepare to travel into Washington for President-elect Barack Obama’s inauguration, one transportation option will take them off the roads and rails entirely: the Potomac River.

The Potomac Riverboat Company has received approval to operate water taxi service for inauguration attendees, providing a maritime alternative for residents who want to avoid expected congestion on highways, bridges and Metro lines. The service is expected to appeal particularly to people traveling from Northern Virginia, where officials are warning of heavy traffic, bridge restrictions and crowded public transit throughout Inauguration Day.

The company’s water taxis will operate under tight federal security rules established for the event. The U.S. Coast Guard has created a maritime security zone on the Potomac and Anacostia rivers as part of the broader inauguration security plan. Access to the zone will be limited, and only vessels with proper authorization will be permitted to operate in restricted areas.

The security zone is intended to protect waterfront areas near the capital during the inauguration, when hundreds of thousands of people are expected to gather in Washington. Recreational boaters and unauthorized vessels will be barred from entering controlled portions of the rivers, and law enforcement boats will patrol the area.

For passengers, the approved water taxi service could provide a less conventional but potentially smoother trip into the city. However, riders are being urged to plan ahead, arrive early and expect security procedures similar to those in place across the region.

Transportation officials have encouraged inauguration visitors to use public transit where possible, but they have also warned that Metro parking lots, trains and stations may reach capacity. Many bridges from Virginia into Washington will have restrictions, and some roadways will be closed to private vehicles.

The water taxi option adds another route for Virginia residents determined to witness the historic swearing-in of the nation’s first Black president. Still, officials stress that river travel will be closely controlled and that passengers should use only approved services.

Anyone planning to travel by water is advised to confirm schedules, ticketing and boarding locations directly with the Potomac Riverboat Company before Inauguration Day.
